is: The HTTP driving adapter over `composition::Runtime`: the axum router, the RFC 9457 error shape, the generated wire contract, the session layer, and the one background task — handlers are thin drivers over the shared `application::*` use cases (`commissions/channel` + `commissions/elements` still await a use case, and `session`'s sign-in provisioning still opens its own unit of work).
conventions: Two endpoint shapes coexist — the browser sign-in flow redirects; every JSON API returns status codes (401, never a redirect).
Errors are `application/problem+json` with a `urn:zurfur:error:*` type and terse code.
A namespace boundary is a policy boundary: cookie-surface routers sit under the first-party-Origin CSRF layer; `/health` and a future bearer `/plugin/v1` mount outside it by construction.
Session→identity resolution is one axum extractor, `extract::CallingUser`, never a per-module helper.
Parity tests (`create_account_parity.rs`, `delete_account_parity.rs`, `whoami_parity.rs`) pin this driver's projections identical to the CLI's until the contract moves to a leaf crate.

The `dev-profile` Cargo feature alone chooses the dev profile (never config or `.env`). Two locks: `main` refuses unless `ZURFUR_ENV` is set and names dev, and `dev_profile::app` refuses a resolved environment other than `DEV`, both before anything starts. `just gate`, gate-light and CI lint and test the feature in `target/dev-profile` (so `target/debug/api` is never the profile), pinned by `scripts/dev-profile-pins.test.sh`.

fs.name: Cargo.toml
fs.role: wires domain + adapter-pg + composition + application + shared, tokio-util/futures-util for upload streaming glue (adapter-mem/test-support/contract-gen/cli as dev-deps); sqlx only for the sweeper's advisory lock; the `dev-profile` feature (off by default) makes adapter-mem a real dependency and builds the dev profile into the binary

fs.name: src/
fs.role: lib/main, logging (the server subscriber with the shared DNS-client filter), extractors, routes, problem, sweep, generated contract types

fs.name: tests/
fs.role: ~40 flat integration suites over reqwest (accounts, commissions/*, csrf, session_fixation, cross_persona_unlinkability, golden_wire, den_golden (writes and drift-checks contract/golden/den), contract_current, e2e, postgres_setup (the app on PostgreSQL via test_support::pg_app), den (the den routes on the in-memory fixture world) and den_postgres (the same routes on PostgreSQL over test_support::pg_app::den_world, the one 404 for every pair of causes), commission_reads_postgres (the changelog read and the download behind den's check on PostgreSQL: each pair of not-found causes answers byte for byte alike and reads alike), den_postgres_accounts (identity's Accounts through the Den on PostgreSQL: a deactivated Account only to its Owner, equal store calls for another's and a missing Account, no answer naming another user, a refused stored name shown as its handle, founding refusing it with the 422), not_found_statements (every pair of not-found causes at the same depth runs the same SQL statements in the same order, read off the wire by test_support::pg_app's statement proxy, from a warm and a cold profile cache), not_found_timing (ignored: each pair's clock times for the security review, `just den-timing`), identity_reads_behind_den (GET /accounts and GET /me behind den's access check on both stacks, over test_support::store_doubles), dev_profile (the default-build guards in every build; with the feature, the environment lock, the fixed sign-in, sessions not crossing stacks, and the real binary), plus CLI/API parity tests create_account_parity/delete_account_parity/whoami_parity) + tests/common/mod.rs assert_problem

notes: Cross-persona unlinkability: no route may join one person's separate handles/Users as the same human (holds by construction — separate handle → separate User → separate DID); guarded by `tests/cross_persona_unlinkability.rs`.
The cookie surface also carries `Cache-Control: no-store` (beyond CSRF) so authenticated identity/PII JSON is never cached (CWE-525).

Logging (`src/logging.rs`): `main` installs `logging::subscriber` — `RUST_LOG`, else the config's `log_level`, over formatted stdout — with `composition::logging`'s filter layer on top, which drops every event from the DNS client's crates (`hickory_resolver`, `hickory_net`, `hickory_proto`) whatever the filter says, because hickory logs the name it was asked about (a handle's domain) at `error` on a malformed answer. The CLI layers the same filter. Pinned by `logging/tests.rs`.

`src/generated/*.rs` still carries DD pointers in its doc comments: it is generated from `contract/*.proto`, so the fix belongs on the `.proto` field comments, not here — a hand-edit would be regenerated away.
